channel.title: Organized Culturality — Texts
channel.description: Reviews and reflections on films, plays, music, and concerts.

item.title: European Cultural Studies in Favour of the Glorious Palestinian People, or "It Must Be Heaven"
item.description: Elia Suleiman made a film whose hero changes almost nothing — which is exactly what leaves you alone with your own conclusions.

item.title: Two on a Swing: Where Am I in This, and Am I Wanted
item.description: Not a recommendation but an attempt to think it through — written straight after the run at the Lensoviet Theatre.

item.title: Looking for Inspiration, or How to Live Among Robots and Keep Your Head
item.description: How "Robot Kostya" came about — Russia's first robotic theatre production, where it turned out Chekhovian passions were within a robot's range after all.

item.title: Vera Polozkova — "High Resolution"
item.description: Poems that find more breath in the music each time round, and end up better listening than most songs.

item.title: How to Keep Your Head in This World — The Queen's Gambit, by the Rules and Otherwise
item.description: "The Queen's Gambit" made chess reachable even for people who've held a queen maybe twice in their lives.

item.title: In the Eye of the Beholder, or Dom Radio — Irrational and Grand
item.description: Since Teodor Currentzis arrived, Dom Radio has become the city's fixed point. On a building you walk into in order to come out different.

item.title: Currentzis. Knew, Saw, Felt
item.description: Debussy, Ravel, Stravinsky and Satie in one evening at the Philharmonic — and a hall that came back to life along with the music.

item.title: Watching From the Bottom, or "Annette" — a Serious Conversation, Arriving on Time
item.description: Leos Carax's film, in which the end of the story isn't the end of it — everybody sets their own.

item.title: A Force You Envy and Bow To — Maya Plisetskaya
item.description: The moment where the question of age stops applying: she's fifty, and she's outside time.

item.title: Gerda, or a Breath of Air That Freezes Mid-Flight — But Does It Land?
item.description: Natalia Kudryashova's film — written in verse, about a city held down by snow, and about whether you're ready to get off the ground.

item.title: Everyone in General Is Pitiful, No One in Particular, or "Medea" — For Us, About Us, Against Us?
item.description: Alexander Zeldovich's film, where the words don't compete with the music — and one question is left standing: do you understand me?

item.title: Interview V, or You Don't Pick Your Times — You Live in Them
item.description: Vertinsky in the flesh on the Seventh Tier of the Alexandrinsky — and the question of how defenceless a person is, and how far shut inside their own body.

item.title: No Need to Write
item.description: On art not always saving you — and on trying to simply carry on living.

item.title: Screening Diary: Liminal Spaces and a Festival Run
item.description: Several short verdicts in a row, from "Hoppers" to the backrooms — and why the liminal-space trend works right up until somebody explains it.

item.title: "Michael" — Impressive, and It Plays Like a Party Broadcast
item.description: Watched it for free, and it does impress: serious money, a conflict that's properly built. But the context behind the accusations has been wiped.

item.title: "Shurale" — a Hope That Came Apart
item.description: Good cast, beautiful images, and the film still comes apart. On stepping behind the camera too early.

item.title: A Film With a Killer Turn, Seen at Dom Radio
item.description: The credits roll halfway through, and that turns out to be the whole point. On an elderly couple, flowers, and the premium version of ascending.

item.title: Antonioni's "Red Desert" — Cinema You Feel Rather Than Follow
item.description: His first film in colour, where even the colour he had wasn't enough — and the subject turned out to be a crisis of everything.

item.title: The New Ozon — Beautifully Shot, as Ever
item.description: A black-and-white film that ends with the hero losing his head but not his point. One of the few reasons to go to Dom Radio for something like this.

item.title: The New Jarmusch — Possibly Just Not My Film
item.description: Everything sits where it should and the moves are good, and there's still a sense he's simply got old.

item.title: Nikolai Kolyada's "Hamlet" — Physically Filthy Theatre on the Edge of Kitsch
item.description: A world about to disappear, turned into an enormous tip. Not theatre for the casual, and half a manifesto for the theatregoer hidden inside a review.

item.title: "The Admirer" — When a Soviet Classic Burns Out
item.description: A serious cast, a cinematographer who shot Balabanov — and the film still goes after your tears with a cheaply built romance.

item.title: "The Heavenly Tapper" — a Documentary Declaration of Love for Karavaichuk
item.description: A brilliant Soviet pianist and composer the Ministry of Culture is in no hurry to show anyone, despite having paid for the film.

item.title: Nigina Sayfullaeva's "Fidelity" — More Bad Than Good
item.description: A cast with no inhibitions, ready for anything in the name of art — and a film that drowns in a claim to meanings that were never there.

item.title: "The Irishman" — Three and a Half Hours of a Classic People Will Keep Going Back To
item.description: Scorsese, a de-aged De Niro and Pacino, 309 scenes across 170 locations — and a hero who simply goes with the current, having no further use for a soul.

item.title: "Beware of Pity" and "Close People" — When the Director Beats the Text, and When He Doesn't
item.description: McBurney got the better of Zweig without quite showing how. Bondar didn't get the better of Vodolazkin, or of the small stage either.

item.title: The New Lopushansky — Almost a Straight "Gentle Creature"
item.description: Expected another round of Russian misery, got a literary and religious story worthy of Dostoevsky. Maxim Sukhanov gives the best performance in Russian cinema this year.

item.title: "The Very Same Munchausen" and "Marriage Story" — On Nobody Wanting to Hear Anybody
item.description: The problem of tolerance sits above every other problem we have. Zakharov was shouting about it under Soviet censorship; it only rings louder now.

item.title: Gaspar Noé's "Love" — Art Either Arrives on Time or Not at All
item.description: Armchair critics called it pornography for intellectuals, and it was kept out of Russian cinemas. On landing in the wrong world for you — or the wrong year.

item.title: "Euphoria" — a Show About Drugs That Is Actually About Not Being Heard
item.description: A portrait of the modern person who prefers a screen to being in the room — and what that costs.

item.title: "Following the White Rabbit" — the Therapeutic Value of a Second Text About the Same Play
item.description: The second post I've written about one Roma Kaganovich production, because reciting the same stock phrases about quality is too crude a thing to do.

item.title: "Philosophers" at Lyubimovka — a Reading That Never Became a Production
item.description: During the young playwrights' festival, Teatr.doc comes apart at the seams with nerves and delight — and the best of these readings can be watched from anywhere.

item.title: Teodor Ioannovich and the Contemporary Viewer's Workshop
item.description: Currentzis turned Perm from a provincial backwater into a cultural centre — and was then sent off to the city where he'd been a student.

item.title: "The Elder Son" — a Production That No Longer Exists on Video
item.description: The Lensoviet Theatre never released a recording of Yuri Butusov's production. It has to be remembered through footage kind people put up themselves.

item.title: "Jojo Rabbit" — a Film About Nazism I Liked Far More Than Expected
item.description: Taika Waititi plays Hitler as a ten-year-old's imaginary friend — and the result is that rare thing, a form fused properly to its content.

item.title: Rimas Tuminas's "Uncle Vanya" — a Production That Works Even on Video
item.description: Ten years on, some of the devices already look archaic — and the catharsis still arrives, even through a screen.

item.title: Theodoros Terzopoulos's "Mauser" — Theatre of the Body, Live on Air
item.description: The Alexandrinsky streamed the premiere, and it turned my whole idea of theatre on video around. I understood about twenty per cent of it, which was plenty.

item.title: Noise and Anti-Noise — Evgeny Voronovsky's Lecture, Which Needed Time to Land
item.description: On the physics of sound turned into a form of art — and on a place you can't download, only walk into and feel.
